info: Before and After situations. Each pair (B1/A1, B2/A2 ...) measures the same values with a different situation. Scores: respect, understanding, kindness, caring, compassion.

before.text: A new student joins your class and sits alone during lunch. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Continue talking with my friends.
Invite the student to join us.
Wait until someone else talks to them.
Ask whether they want company.

before.text: Your friend gets a bad mark on a test and is quiet all day. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Say: “Don't worry, it's just one test.”
Ask how they feel and really listen.
Leave them alone. It's not my business.
Offer to study together next time.

before.text: A classmate shares an idea in class, and some students laugh at it. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Laugh with the others.
Say: “Let them finish. I want to hear the idea.”
Stay quiet.
Later, tell them their idea was interesting.

before.text: Your little brother or sister breaks your favourite thing by accident and starts crying. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Shout at them.
Tell them it's okay — accidents happen.
Ask what happened before I react.
Ignore them for the rest of the day.

before.text: A classmate who uses a wheelchair can't reach a book on a high shelf. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Grab the book for them without asking.
Ask if they would like some help.
Walk past. They'll manage.
Help, and suggest to the teacher that books go on lower shelves.

before.text: Someone in your group project isn't doing their part because their family is going through a hard time. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Tell the teacher they are lazy.
Try to understand and share the tasks differently.
Do their part quietly, but feel annoyed.
Ask them privately how I can support them.

before.text: A friend tells you a secret and asks you not to share it. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Tell just one other close friend.
Keep the secret.
Keep the secret and ask if they are okay.
Make a joke about it later.

before.text: An elderly neighbour is carrying heavy shopping bags up the stairs. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Pretend I didn't see.
Offer to carry a bag.
Smile and say hello.
Ask if they need help and walk up with them.

after.text: At summer camp, one child doesn't know anyone and stands alone by the fence. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Keep playing my game.
Wave them over to join my group.
Hope a camp leader notices them.
Go over, say hi, and ask if they'd like to join.

after.text: Your teammate missed an easy goal, and your team lost. Now they sit alone. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Say: “Forget it, it's just a game.”
Sit next to them and ask how they feel.
Go home with the others.
Offer to practise together this week.

after.text: A quiet student answers a question with an accent, and some students copy the way they talk. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Copy the accent too. It's funny.
Say: “Stop it. Let them speak.”
Look away and say nothing.
After class, tell them I liked their answer.

after.text: Your friend spills juice all over your new notebook by accident and looks scared. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Yell at them.
Say it's fine and ask if they're okay.
Ask what happened before getting upset.
Stop talking to them for a while.

after.text: A classmate with a broken arm is trying to open a heavy door. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Open it for them without a word.
Ask: “Do you want me to get that?”
Wait for them to manage on their own.
Help, and offer to carry their bag this week.

after.text: Your friend stopped answering messages after their pet died. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Decide they're being rude.
Understand they're grieving and give them space, with a kind note.
Keep sending funny videos as usual.
Write: “I'm here if you want to talk.”

after.text: A friend shows you a drawing they feel shy about and asks you not to show anyone. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Show the class — it's really good!
Keep it private.
Keep it private and tell them it was brave to share.
Take a photo of it to post later.

after.text: A little child is lost and crying in a shop. What would you most likely do?

options.text: Walk away. Someone else will help.
Stay with them and tell a shop worker.
Smile at them as I pass.
Kneel down, ask their name, and calmly help find their parent.
